content.thinking:
Some failures are expected mislabeled? "Assume Feb can have up to 29 in all years, without distinguishing leap years" means 2023-02-29 should be valid! My test expected [] is wrong. Good regex.

Boundary: "not immediately preceded or followed by alphanumeric characters." Underscore and hyphen are not alphanumeric. So `2024-01-01_` and `2024-01-01-` dates are valid by stated boundary. My expected [] was wrong. So regex fine. Need maybe think more deeply about hidden tests and whether any flaw.

Could maybe use simpler regex with captures? We have one capture group. Fine.

Need ensure `re.findall` with pattern containing one capture group returns dates. Yes.

Need understand requirements precisely:
"Write a regex expression that matches dates in the format YYYY-MM-DD appearing in lines that contain an IPv4 address in a log file."
Could mean match date if line contains IPv4 address (anywhere). We handle.
"If multiple dates are present in a line, the regex should match only the last date in that line." We handle one match last.
"Assume that February can have up to 29 days in all years, without distinguishing leap years from non-leap years." We allow Feb29 all years. Fine.
"IPv4 addresses use normal decimal notation without leading zeros in each octet." We validate.
